title: Your weekly trade review is missing a step

channel.name: Andrew Builds (TradeNotes)
channel.appBlurb: a trading journal and performance analytics app

body.hook: Your weekly trade review is missing a step. Probably the important one.
body.promise: It is a ten-minute loop with three steps. The third is the one people skip.

beats.narration: Step one: find the leak. Sort the week by tag and pick the habit that shows up most.
Step two: question the fix. Backtest the rule that would have blocked it. That shows history, not what will happen.

scene.label: Step 2: rule to test
scene.text: No new trade for 30 minutes after a loss.
scene.caption: History, not a prediction.

beats.narration: Step three, the skipped one: write the rule where you will see it before Monday's first trade.
Here is why. Next week's review starts with one count: the days you followed it.
I built TradeNotes, my own trading journal, so I'm biased. It keeps your tags and notes in one place for that review.
So the journal finds the leak, the backtest questions the fix, the review closes it. None of that removes the risk of loss. It keeps you honest.

body.cta: Set a ten-minute timer this weekend and run the loop once. Not financial advice.

promise.sub: The third is the one people skip.

cta.title: TradeNotes
cta.tagline: Ten-minute timer. This weekend. Run the loop once.

A backtest shows what a rule did historically (hypothetical, not a prediction), and nothing here removes the risk of loss. I built TradeNotes, so I'm biased. Educational content only, not financial advice.
